title: Pochettino to land Lucas Moura for Spurs but rues market ‘realities’
trail: Mauricio Pochettino said Tottenham need to make opportunistic strikes in the transfer market as he prepared to welcome  Brazil’s winger Lucas Moura from Paris Saint-Germain for £25m
body: Mauricio Pochettino has stressed the need for Tottenham Hotspur to make opportunistic strikes on the transfer market, as he prepared to welcome the Brazilian winger Lucas Moura from Paris Saint-Germain for £25m. The manager mentioned Manchester United’s signing of Alexis Sánchez and Manchester City’s club record £57.2m deal for Aymeric Laporte to illustrate his point that Spurs were operating under “different realities” when compared to the game’s financial heavyweights. Pochettino hopes the situation can begin to change when Tottenham switch to their new £850m stadium next season but for now, he must move for players that the elite do not or no longer want. Moura is an example. When he was available from São Paulo in 2012, he was tracked by a host of the biggest clubs, including United. In the end, PSG completed a £38m deal for him and he joined in January 2013. It was not a race that Tottenham could enter. This season, the 25-year-old has fallen from favour at PSG following the arrivals of Neymar and Kylian Mbappe – he has not started a single game for them – and, with the elite-level clubs looking elsewhere, Tottenham have seen a deal with potential. “We are a club where we sign opportunities,” Pochettino said. “Manchester United want Alexis and so they go for him. It’s like this. I don’t say that it’s good or it’s bad. I only say that we are different. We are in different positions and different realities. Manchester City pay the buyout clause in [Athletic] Bilbao [for Laporte] and bring the player that they want. Tottenham is not this type of club. “When we signed Heung-min Son [from Bayer Leverkusen], it was at the end of the window [in August 2015.] We tried from the beginning. First of all, he said no. Then, he struggled to play and was upset with the manager, they opened the door and we signed him. Because it was an opportunity. Understand the difference. Fernando Llorente was an opportunity on the last day of the window last summer. Yes or no?”
